paragraphs: One Morning, Four Messages, posted by May. Our school has a radio morning in the hall. Every group has a job. Teacher Kim and the Explorers plan the morning. It starts at nine o'clock. I wrote four messages about the event. Each one is for a different reader. Can you find the reader of each message? Look at the first words and at the way the message talks.

Message One is a poster on the library door. It says, "Hey, kids! Do you want to talk into a microphone?" The reader is a child, because the poster says "kids". The words are short, and the voice is friendly. I put it up on Monday, and many children stopped to read it. Leo drew a big green microphone at the bottom.

Message Two is a note from Teacher Kim. It says, "Dear parents, the children will read the news by themselves." The note also says, "If your child cannot come, please send an excuse." The reader is a parent, because the note says "Dear parents" and "your child". The note is polite, and it gives clear instructions. Parents read the note at home, so every word must be easy to understand.

Message Three is a short message to a coach. It says, "Dear Coach Matt, please help the sports group with the football news." It also says, "Please come to the hall at half past eight." The reader is a coach, because the message starts with "Dear Coach Matt". A coach is a teacher for sport, so the message is short and clear. Coach Matt helps the children to read the scores in a loud, clear voice.

Message Four is a notice on the cooking table. It says, "Dear customers, the cooking group sells fresh snacks." The reader is a customer, because the notice says "Dear customers". A snack costs ten baht, and the money goes to the club. The cooking group makes rice cakes and fruit, and the table is always busy. Mia leads the photography group. She takes a photo of each snack.

Every message has a reader, and the reader decides the words. A message for a child is short and funny. A message for a parent or a coach is polite and clear. Leo says that a good writer thinks about the reader first. Which message is for you? Tell us in a comment!
